subject: Operatorless Key Seeding & Transit Lockdown for Private VPC Appliances
messages:
From: Claire Donovan <claire@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security Team <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private appliances: BYOK seeding and strict egress constraints

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and infra teams dug into the private appliance option and we have a couple of hard constraints that will determine whether we can proceed:

- We must perform BYOK with attestable key origin (HSM-backed key generation or split-seed import).
- No outbound egress to public key management endpoints is allowed from the appliance subnets during seeding; any communication must go to our private VPC endpoints or through an approved egress proxy.
- Rotation needs to be operatorless (or operator-minimal) — auditors want documented automated rotation with logged attestations.

Can Redwood support an operatorless key seeding flow (ideally sealed, threshold-based import or remote attestation + wrapped transfer) for an on-prem appliance behind our VPC firewall? Also curious about the transport guarantees, recommended TLS+MTLS profiles, and how the audit trail is surfaced to us (we'll need evidence for SOC 2).

I've attached our initial requirements workbook (acme-byo-reqs-2026.xlsx). Would appreciate a brief design write-up and a 30-min sync next week.

Thanks,
Claire Donovan
Head of Security
Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Claire Donovan <claire@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-04-20T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private appliances: BYOK seeding and strict egress constraints

Hi Claire — appreciate the clear constraints and the workbook. Short answers up front: yes, we can support an operator-minimal seed flow for on-prem appliances that avoids direct public egress, and we can produce auditable rotation records.

High-level options (quick summary):
1) Split-seed partnership: Redwood provides a sealed import tool that accepts a threshold-sliced seed from your on-prem KMS; no part of the seed leaves your control unwrapped. Import occurs over a private peering or via a customer-controlled bastion.
2) Remote attestation + wrapped transport: Appliance performs an attestation (TPM/SE) to Redwood's attestation service over MTLS to a VPC endpoint; Redwood returns a wrapped key blob only after attestation. This can be routed over your private endpoint or through a VPC peering connection.
3) HSM direct-attach (customer-managed): You run an HSM in your VPC and we support transparent integration patterns (KMIP/PKCS11) with zero plaintext egress from your HSM.

I'll attach a short ops note with the expected network flows and required DNS/NAT rules. If you prefer, we can sketch a minimal design for option 2 (attestation + wrapped transport) which is typically the least operationally burdensome for customers that can't host an HSM.

Can we book 30 min on Apr 23 or Apr 27?

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private appliances: BYOK seeding and strict egress constraints

Hannah / Naomi — looping you in to confirm our recommended pattern for Acme. They have strict no-public-egress during seeding and want rotation automation with auditable attestations. My quick sketch attached (kms-vpc-operatorless-sketch.pdf). Key points and questions: 

- Preferred default: remote attestation + wrapped key transport (option 2). Pros: minimal operator work, fits their firewall constraints via VPC endpoint or peered link. Cons: requires an attestation root on the appliance (TPM/SE) and a short-lived bootstrap credential.
- If they insist on zero external dependency at all, split-seed via an onsite HSM is viable but operational heavy.

Network considerations (high-level):
- Inbound: Redwood will NOT initiate unsolicited inbound connections into their VPC. All interactions originate from the appliance to a customer-controlled VPC endpoint (NLB+MTLS).
- Egress: Allowlist required destination: internal NLB address (no public SNAT). If an egress proxy is required, we must agree on mutual auth (client certs) and TLS cipher suites (TLS1.3, AEAD ciphers).
- Audit: We will produce signed rotation events (RFC 3161-like timestamps) plus a TOA (transfer-of-attestation) record and make them available via a customer S3/GCS/GCS-private-bucket push or an on-prem syslog collector over TLS.

Operational gaps we need help from Infra/Security to decide:
- Do they have TPM attestation firmware already deployed on the appliances? If not, we need to propose a bootstrap that uses a short-lived operator action (one-time operator minimal), followed by operatorless rotation thereafter.
- Which audit sink do they prefer (push to customer S3 vs. pull from Redwood API via peered endpoint)?

Please review the attached sketch for recommended port rules and cert life-cycle. If you agree, I'll share the option-2 write-up and a proposed checklist for the customer's infra team.

Thanks — Jordan

--

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private appliances: BYOK seeding and strict egress constraints — recommended plan and next steps

Hi Claire — thanks for the workbook and the patience while we scoped the options internally. Jordan and I validated the attestation + wrapped-transport approach with our infra team and this is our recommended phased plan: 

Phase 1 — One-time bootstrap + Attestation onboarding (2 weeks)\- Appliance makes an outbound MTLS call to your private NLB endpoint to register its attestation certificate. This call is initiated from the appliance; no public egress is required.
- We will provide a small sealed-bootstrap helper (signed by Redwood) that can be run inside your network to generate the initial attestation material if TPM is not present; this requires a single operator step (run + verify) and is logged.

Phase 2 — Wrapped key transfer (2–3 days)\- After successful attestation, Redwood issues a wrapped key blob over the same MTLS channel. The wrapped blob is unwrapped only within the appliance TPM/HSM.
- The transfer is subject to replay protections and has a one-time nonce per transfer.

Phase 3 — Automated rotation and evidence push (ongoing)\- Rotation scheduler on Redwood rotates keys per agreed cadence and pushes signed rotation records to your chosen audit sink (we prefer push to a customer S3/GCS private endpoint over a peered connection). Each rotation record contains a signed TOA and rotation provenance.

Acceptance criteria we need from Acme:
- Confirm NLB endpoint + cert chain we should trust for MTLS (or provide your egress proxy details).
- Which audit sink (S3 bucket ARN or syslog collector FQDN) you want us to push rotation evidence to.
- If you want split-seed instead of attestation, tell us now — otherwise we'll proceed with option 2.

Next steps: Jordan will share a short design doc and a port/cert checklist today. Can we lock a 30-min call on Apr 29 at 10:00 PT to walk through the checklist and sign off?

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
